pages.transcription:
Taft Hotel                                      Newhaven, 13th March 1941.

Dear Jan,

I am sorry that you seem to have misunderstood my letter
to mean that we would be able to help you indefinitely until you had
found a suitable position for yourself. Unfortunately this is not
the case. You must realise that besides all the other obligations
(house, support of former wife, relatives and friends, enormous taxes)
Stefan is now maintaining our mother completely since months. I am
happy that this has been possible and that in these difficult times
I have been able to take over temporarily from you, Manfred and Richard
the care for mother, and I sincerely hope that for the next future I
will be able to continue that. - But that we are now temporarily in
America means in no way a pleasure trip, and Stefan is working hard to
meet both ends, although I purposely have avoided to mention this in my
letters to Mama. Hardly anyone has been so severely hit in his pro-
fessional activity that a Jewish writer whose books are forbidden in
all Europe except England (where nearly the whole stock was burned ~~at~~
the ~~bookbinder~~. And the sales in America have always been but the smallest
part of his former income.

I am sorry that this misunderstanding has arisen, sorry for
you and for Hanna who of course could not dispose of Stefan's money
without instruction from us, after she had given you those £ 35. With
Stefan's consent I am now asking her to-day to let you have once more
£ 20 (twenty pounds) which is all which we can do for you until August.

As to an affidavit for USA I have also no good news for you
much as I had liked to help[?] you. We are unfortunately experts in
this matter as since months Stefan gets letters from relatives and
friends nearly every day. Unfortunately the situation has now become
very difficult. The affidavit-giver, besides many other things has to
show his bank account and income and to undertake a guarantee. And we
have had in the last weeks nothing but refusals, as all our friends have
already given too many or have no money themselves. Should I hear of
anybody, however, I shall of course let you know it at once.

Hoping that you have good news from your wife and that your
own situation will quickly improve,
                                                Lotte

As I do not know whether your address is still the same, I have to
send you this letter through Hanna.
